description_full: Octave Intelligence plc provides various software solutions. Its solutions helps organizations to better understand and manage the environment in which they design, build, operate, and protect their assets, people, and critical infrastructure. Its platform connects data, events, and workflows across various environments and applies context-aware intelligence to help customers understand what is happening, what may happen next, and how actions in one area affect conditions in another. The company chemicals and petrochemicals, electronics, life sciences and pharma, public safety, construction, manufacturing, security, engineering services (EPCs), data centers, food, beverage and retail, metals and mining, transportation, defence, government and public sector, oil and gas, education, healthcare, and power and utilities industries. It operates in the United States, Canada, Latin America, Europe, the Middle East, India, Africa, and rest of APAC region. The company was incorporated in 2017 and is based in Madison, Alabama.
ceo_bio: Mr. Mattias  Stenberg B.Sc., B.Sc. (Econ.) | CEO & Director | Age 48 | Compensation: $1.8M (FY2025)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 7K people. Revenue per employee of $223K ranks in the bottom quartile among Technology peers. Each employee generates $49K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $2K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 8× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). R&D investment of 10% of revenue (moderate) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: Octave Intelligence plc is a mid-cap technology business with a $5.9B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 4% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 71% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $355M in free cash flow — roughly 22 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.61× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 20% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.

sect: Its 24% operating margin runs 18pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.04x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 9% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has rebounded 13% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 27% below the high.
About $35.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.
val: The stock trades 56% below its DCF fair value of $50.13, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 39%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $35.21 to $72.18 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 19.1 vs 27.4 and P/FCF 16.6 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 6.0% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.5% (vs the 8% bar).
The 7 covering analysts target $23.36 on average, 6% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 0.6% annual cash-flow growth, 14pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 4% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.6%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have been steady (CV 0.17).
It runs a 71% gross margin and converts 22% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 8/9 and cash conversion of 1.61x.
ROE of 4% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.1x equity multiplier).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $33.1M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).
Goodwill makes up 72% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 8.3% over 3 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 13.1% on average.
Analysts expect 3.2% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own 19.7%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 16%.
people: With about 7,200 employees, each generates about $223K of revenue, 0.6x the Technology median.
That works out to $49K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.8M (8x revenue per employee).
